Q4 integrated. Last question.

**Question:** When exactly one file is extracted, should the summary line read `extracted 1 files` or `extracted 1 file`?

**Why it matters:** The spec fixes the output as the literal `extracted N files`, and acceptance tests will compare that line character for character — so a test written for grammatical output and an implementation written for the literal template will disagree on the single-file case.

**Recommended:** Option A - The feature description specifies the template `extracted N files` verbatim, and a machine-readable summary line is easier to parse when its shape never changes. Pluralizing adds a special case that earns nothing for a script consumer, which is the primary audience for this line.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Always the literal template: `extracted 1 files`, `extracted 0 files`, `extracted 2 files` — shape never varies |
| B | Grammatically correct: `extracted 1 file` for exactly one, `extracted N files` otherwise |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (<=5 words) |
